deep.reconstruction:
Date and context. 'Sonntag May 3' fits 1818, when May 3 was a Sunday; the next page has 'May 6 Mittwoch'. The setting is Göttingen meridian-instrument work. The page holds two kinds of material.

(A) Observations of 3 May.
(1) Level (Libelle) readings, two rows by three columns, averaged by column:
- (3'21.2+3'16.5)/2 = 3'18.85
- (31.5+27.6)/2 = 29.55
- (13.9+8.3)/2 = 11.10
From these Gauss states the axis inclination i = a + 4.73" (the figure is overwritten).
(2) Transit of the Sun over three wires.
- First limb: 2h38'19.2, 38'36.2, 38'53.2; mean 38'36.20.
- Second limb: 40'31.5, 40'48.2, 41'5.5; mean 40'48.40.
- Centre: (38'36.20+40'48.40)/2 = 2h39'42.30, which is the 'Mittel'.
This is the clock time of the Sun's centre transit. Its value (RA about 2h40m) fits early May. Half the limb interval, 66.1 s, times 15 cos(15.9°) gives about 953", the solar semidiameter.
Also recorded:
- the lower limb on the movable wire ('Unt. R. am b. Fd.'), circle reading 36°16'25.6, with a micrometer value of 1'19.9;
- barometer 27 in 5.45 lines, attached thermometer 12.9°, free-air thermometer 14.2°.
(3) Afternoon level readings, by column:
- (20.89+19.95)/2 = 20.42
- (30.39+29.70)/2 = 30.045 → 30.04
- (12.79+11.30)/2 = 12.045 → 12.04
These give i = a + 1.04".

(B) Reduction of the α Hydrae zenith distance (observed on the previous page) and a latitude derived from it.
Gauss tabulates the correction (apparent − mean) to the zenith distance z = φ − δ, so every term is −Δδ. The reference is the mean place for 1819.0, for May 1, 11, 21, 31. The Sun's longitudes are ⊙ = 40°40', 50°19', 59°55', 69°28', and the Moon's node runs from Ω = 38°43' to 37°08'.
- Aberration: +10^0.9942 · sin(⊙ + 77°37'), i.e. 9.867" × sin(118°17', 127°56', 137°32', 147°05'). The logs 9.9448, 9.8969, 9.8294, 9.7351 give +8.69, +7.78, +6.66, +5.36. Check (mine): for α ≈ 139.7°, δ ≈ −7.87° and κ ≈ 20.25", −Δδ_ab = +9.86 sin(⊙ + 77.6°).
- Lunar nutation: 10^0.9193 · sin(Ω + 228°45') = 8.304" × (logs 9.9996n … 9.9989n), giving −8.30, −8.29, −8.29, −8.28. This equals −(5.47 sin Ω + 6.24 cos Ω). That matches −(Δψ sinε cosα + Δε sinα) with Δψ ≈ 18.0" and Δε ≈ 9.6", the nutation constants then current.
- Solar (semi-annual) nutation: 10^(9.670−10) · sin(2⊙ + 223°) = 0.468" × sin, with 2⊙ = 81°20', 100°38', 119°50', 138°56'. The logs 9.917n, 9.773n, 9.470n, 8.528 give −0.39, −0.28, −0.14, +0.02.
- Precession from date to 1819.0: annual rate log 1.18611 (15.35"), divided by log 2.56259 (365.25 d), gives 0.04203"/day (log 8.62352). Times the days left to 1819.0, log 2.38696 (243.75 d) on May 1 and log 2.33009 (213.8 d) on May 31, this gives −10.24 … −8.99. Intermediate values are −9.82 and −9.41.
- Sum of the four columns: −10.24, −10.61, −11.18, −11.89 (all verified).
- Refraction: log factors 9.99310 (thermometer) + 9.99441 (barometer: 27 in 7.7 lines / 28 in) + 1.98945 (mean refraction 97.60" ≈ 57.7" tan 59°23') give log 1.97696, i.e. 94.83".
- Reduction chain: observed z = 59°23'11.92; plus refraction 94.83" gives 59°24'46.75; plus 10.24" (reduction of the May 1 apparent place to the mean place 1819.0) gives 59°24'56.99.
- Declination: Pond's 1815 catalogue mean gives δ = −7°51'43.0. Four years of precession, −61.36", gives δ(1819.0) = −7°52'44.36. A first attempt written '−7°51'98.34' is crossed out.
- Latitude: φ = z + δ = 59°24'56.99 − 7°52'44.36 = 51°32'12.63. Gauss wrote this as '51°31'12"63'. It is to be compared with 51°32'14.77 (previous page) and 51°32'8.64 (next page).
errors: Crossed-out intermediate −7°51'98.34: 43.0 + 61.36 = 104.36, so the correct result is −7°52'44.36. Gauss corrected it.
The final latitude appears as 51°31'12"63, but 59°24'56.99 − 7°52'44.36 = 51°32'12.63. Either this is a writing slip or the image reads 32. The neighbouring pages give 51°32'.

The header constant of the solar-nutation column reads '222', but the logarithms 9.917, 9.773, 9.470, 8.528 are matched exactly only by 2⊙ + 223°. With 222° the values would be 9.922, 9.783, 9.494, 8.21. So the figure is 223 (or overwritten).
Four years of precession at 15.35"/yr is 61.40", while Gauss uses 61.36 (15.34"/yr). This is a negligible difference, possibly a slightly different rate.
The inclination figure 4"73 is overwritten. The derivation of i from the level readings is not shown.

results.what: Meridian transit of the Sun from the two limbs over three wires (clock time of the centre transit)
Reduction of a zenith distance from apparent to mean place: aberration A sin(⊙+B), lunar nutation C sin(Ω+D), solar nutation E sin(2⊙+F), and linear precession to 1819.0
results.modern_name: reduction to mean place (Besselian-type star constants)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration 1729, nutation 1748); tabular forms by Delambre, Zach, Bessel

results.what: Refraction from mean refraction (~57.7" tan z) times barometric and thermometric factors
Latitude of Göttingen from the meridian zenith distance of α Hydrae and Pond's 1815 declination
results.modern_name: latitude determination from meridian zenith distances

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observing-log page. It records level readings, a solar transit and a textbook reduction of a star's zenith distance (aberration, nutation, precession, refraction) to obtain the observatory latitude. Gauss's Göttingen observing work of 1818–19 is well documented.

transcription_corrections: The solar-nutation header '222' is evidently 223 (or 222 overwritten to 223), judging by the logarithms.
The final latitude '51°31'12"63' should arithmetically be 51°32'12"63.
The rows under 0.9193 carry node longitudes 38°43' to 37°08' (intermediate rows blank). The arguments under 222/223 are 2⊙: 81°20', 100°38', 119°50', 138°56'.
The angles in the first column are in degrees and minutes (40°40', 50°19', 59°55', 69°28' = Sun's longitude; 77°37' = constant), not decimals.
'Mutter [?] proportional [?]' is probably a marginal note on interpolation ('proportional').
The Barom entry is 27 Zoll 5.45 Linien; 'Th. 12"9' is the thermometer at 12.9°, not seconds.
